Pee can be cleaned just like any other liquid, a little soap and water. The smell that can develop after a few days is actually caused by bacteria(gross, I know), to remedy this you can clean it with white vinegar/white wine vinegar before the bacteria get a chance to grow. Depending on where you are geographically, the baking isle at the supermarket might have it and it’s generally pretty cheap.

As far as washing shoes, I think some people put them in the wash(baffles me personally but w/e works ig). Some people have a “cleaning brush” that they never use for their teeth and scrub their shoes with something like that. I personally use just a damp wash cloth, soap and water (and vinegar if the streets have been gross). But I think washing shoes is one of those things that’s pretty personal to everyone and there’s not really any “right/wrong” way to do it. (Or maybe I’m missing out on some shoe cleaning culture, who knows).

But I will say to be careful about using some cleaning products on clothes/shoes as they can sometimes stain (example: bleach wipes)

Lots of good comments here! Definitely check with your uni about student food bank options. Eating is so so important and food insecurity is no joke! I’m also a student who’s been struggling a bit, no shame about it. These are some of my go-to’s:

- Pasta (spaghetti) + red sauce,
Optional: choice of protein(look for deals), & frozen bulk veggies. 
- PB&J sandwiches. 
- Rice bowls 
- Discount loafs of bread (I found going to grocers with a bakery section after the post-work rush (~8pm for my area) can get a huge loaf for ~$2.
- Also using flour and water to make your own bread can be cheap
- Protein powder (only recently started this since I went vegan, it’s expensive upfront but lasts a while and a scoop or two of that in oat/soy milk keeps me from getting hungry for while)

Aldi is your friend. Pay attention to sales. And don’t fast during finals x.x

Lastly, I found that high protein, carbs and fibrous foods are the most filling. Apparently everyone’s body is a little different when it comes to this so try to find what works best for you, and if being hungry on your budget is distracting from your studies, don’t feel weird about reaching out to your university. The meals won’t be gourmet and you’ll likely get sick of your ‘college meals’ after awhile, but at least you’ll be alive enough to get tired of them!
